evidence: RULE 1: a MEASURED offset must exist as its OWN ROW. Recording a measurement inside another row's evidence prose does not reach the resolver. Rows starting with # are skipped by jlc_rotation_resolve.py.

RULE 2 (2026-07-25, THE CORRECTION BELOW): NEVER populate a row from jlc_twin's jlc_offset. Derive it from the BOARD + JLC's cached model with an operator VERIFIED against pcbnew itself (pad.GetFPRelativePosition() vs pad.GetPosition()). jlc_twin.xform() used the wrong handedness, so every offset it reported was NEGATED: invisible at 0/180 (sign-invariant) and exactly 180deg wrong at 90/270. Six rows here were populated from it and were all 180deg wrong. Checker and checked must not share a method (canon M1).

RULE 3 (2026-07-25, canon A-POL): the `polarity` column is a REQUIRED DECLARATION, one of n/a | two-channel | single-channel. A pad-NUMBER fit structurally CANNOT detect a model whose own numbering differs from ours, and a HIGH FIT MARGIN IS NOT CONFIDENCE: on usb-hub-3s-v3's indicator LEDs (C2296/C2297) the pad-number fit returns 180 with a 17.7x margin and is WRONG — JLC numbers pad 1 = ANODE while KiCad Device:LED is pin 1 = K, both libraries draw the cathode WEST, so the true offset is 0 and a 180 row would ship every indicator dark (indistinguishable from a bad joint). two-channel = a NUMBERING-FREE channel (silk chamfer, pin-1 dot/glyph, mounting-tab position, body/courtyard asymmetry, lead axis) is RECORDED IN THIS ROW. single-channel = no such channel exists; the row MUST name the JLC order-preview human gate, which then carries it before first order. Graded by jlc_rotation_audit.py --table.

AP2112K-family LDO in SOT-89-5; crow-recorder-central-v2 U10. THE PAD-NUMBER FIT ALONE IS NOT SUFFICIENT HERE and was flagged as such: a numbering-free fit by pad SIZE CLASS is DEGENERATE at 1.0x (spread 0.0000mm at ALL FOUR angles) because the SOT-89-5 land is its own 180-degree reflection — pads 1,3 at x=-1.85 and 4,5 at x=+1.85 with the tab centred at (0,0). The NUMBERING-FREE channel that does decide it is the PIN-1 BODY MARKING, matched mark-to-mark: our F.Fab chamfer cuts the -x/-y corner at (-1.250,-2.250), JLC's F.SilkS pin-1 dot sits at (+2.26,+2.25) with a second Cmts.User pin-1 circle at (+2.09,+1.51) in the same quadrant. Rotating JLC's mark: 180 lands it 1.0100mm from our chamfer corner vs 2.7646mm for the next best (90) = 2.7x; 0 is 5.0292mm away. Both channels therefore say 180 and they agree. GCT USB4105 16P top-mount USB-C receptacle; crow-recorder-central-v2 J2. Measured 2026-07-25 against JLC's cached TYPE-C-SMD_SBC-160S1A-20-S412 with the pcbnew-verified operator. CHANNELS DISAGREE, and this row is the cleanest demonstration in the table of why canon A-POL exists. The PAD-NUMBER fit says 90 (rms 4.4723mm vs 4.8841mm next = 1.1x, i.e. garbage) because it pairs OUR signal pads 1-4 against JLC's SHELL POSTS, which JLC numbers 1-4 while naming the signal contacts A1/B12/A4/... — the two libraries number different physical features, exactly the failure mode a numbered fit structurally cannot see. The NUMBERING-FREE channel is the shell-post pad SIZE CLASS (no pad number is read; the classes are grouped by their long dimension alone): at offset 0 the 2.1mm-class posts demand dy = -3.105 - (-1.810) = -1.2950 and the 1.8mm-class posts demand dy = +1.075 - (+2.370) = -1.2950 — SELF-CONSISTENT to 0.0000mm, spread 0.0100mm overall; at 180 the same two classes demand -4.915 vs +3.445, an 8.36mm self-contradiction; 90/270 are excluded by the 8.64mm post span against the 4.18mm contact-row span (spread 4.2085mm). Separation 420x. BELIEVE THE NUMBERING-FREE CHANNEL: offset 0. board_rot 0 => correct CPL 0.0. J2 MUST ALSO PASS THE JLC ORDER-PREVIEW human gate before the first order, because the two channels disagreed. Related but separate defect: sealed v1.4 placed this same connector at the KiCad ANCHOR rather than the pad-array centre, 1.3025mm off against 1.150mm contacts = 0.000mm pad overlap (canon A-POS).

SMA-package rectifier diode (POLARIZED, 2-pad collinear); crow-recorder-central-v2 D1. Measured 2026-07-25 against JLC's SMA_L4.3-W2.6-LS5.2-RD with the pcbnew-verified operator. That is exactly the channel canon A-POL proves can be confidently wrong (C2296/C2297: 17.7x margin, wrong answer). NUMBERING-FREE channel, the SILK/FAB CATHODE MARKING, read as SHAPES on both sides: OURS — the KiCad D_SMA F.Fab diode glyph has its cathode BAR at x=-0.649 and its triangle APEX at x=-0.649 with the base at x=+0.501 (a diode triangle points at its cathode), and the F.SilkS cathode band runs the full height at x=-3.510; so OUR cathode is the -x end. Both libraries draw the cathode WEST => the physical parts already align => offset 0, and this agrees with the pad-number fit. board_rot 0 => correct CPL 0.0.
